content:
Apple has raised the subscription price of Apple Music in the United States and several other countries today. Effective immediately, the monthly fee for the Apple Music Individual plan has increased from the original US$10.99 to US$11.99.

Apple has also raised the prices of some Apple One bundle plans.

In a statement to 9to5Mac, Apple said: "Due to rising licensing costs, Apple Music is adjusting its subscription pricing effective today."

Apple Music and Apple One prices raised again

Below are the latest monthly fees for Apple Music and Apple One, effective today:

Apple Music

  • Individual plan: US$11.99 (previously US$10.99)
  • Family plan: US$19.99 (previously US$16.99)
  • Student plan: US$6.99 (previously US$5.99)

Apple One

  • Individual plan: US$19.95 (unchanged)
  • Family plan: US$27.95 (previously US$25.95)
  • Premier plan: US$39.95 (previously US$37.95)

Before Apple Music's price hike, Spotify had already announced a round of price increases earlier this year, which Apple had mocked on social media at the time. However, even after this latest increase, Apple Music's monthly fee remains cheaper than Spotify's.

This is Apple's first Apple Music price increase in nearly four years. The last time Apple raised prices was in October 2022, when the Apple Music Individual plan went from US$9.99 to US$10.99, and Apple One prices were also raised at the same time.

In October 2023, Apple also raised the fees for Apple TV, Apple Arcade, and Apple News+, along with the associated Apple One bundle plans.

Apple TV had another price increase in August 2025, but Apple One prices remained unchanged at that time.
